full_judgment:
2. The plaintiff respondent opposite party No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1989 for prohibitory permanent injunction against the defendant appellant petitioner and defendant respondent-proforma-opposite party Nos. 2-4 alleging, inter alia, that the plaintiff respondent opposite party No. 1 has a 2 storied residential building on the CS plot No.860 as stated in the schedule of the plaint and to the contiguous north of the said residential building situates the pathway on the CS plot No. 862. On both sides of this pathway there situate the residential houses and this is a very thickly populated residential area of the town. It was further stated in the plaint that to the north of the said pathway there, among other plots, situates CS plot No. 865 wherein the defendants have been running a Bakery/Factory known as "Shahin Bakery and Confectionery" for the production of various types of biscuits, cakes, loafs and other confectioneries. The plaintiff further alleged that the defendants have decided to shift the said Baker/Factory from the said plot i.e. c.s plot No. 865 to CS plot No. 861 which is mentioned in the 3rd schedule of the plaint and the said plot situates to the south of the said pathway. This CS plot No.861 belongs to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. So all the defendants conjointly have now decided to start a Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No. 861 which situates to the contiguous west of the plaintiffs residential building on CS plot No.860. Besides, the plaintiffs chamber situates on CS plot No. 859 to the east of his residential building at a distance of about 43 feet therefrom. The further case of the plaintiff is that in residential area the defendants have decided to establish a well organised in shape and size Bakery on the CS plot No. 861 for the production of biscuits, cakes, loafs and confectioneries of various types and for the production of which various kinds of chemicals like ammonia, baking power and raw materials including flour, rotten eggs, sugar and mews (rotten water) etc. are required to be used being mingled together for the purpose of production of the aforesaid item of bakery from the furnace, the brick built fire place which will day and night generate and emit heat, smoke, bad smell and undesirable noise polluting the area. The residence of other people of the locality also situate very thickly in close proximity on both the sides of the said pathway. From the time of human habitation in this locality this has been the residential area of the town of Brahmanbaria. Never it was/is an industrial/commercial area for the establishment of any Industry/Factory, etc. So it exists and will continue to exist as the pure and simple residential area being the part of Kazipara Mahalla of Brahmanbaria town. Kazipara is one of the oldest residential areas of the town. 

 3. The plaintiff further asserted that he has been living with his family members in his said residential building like others of the locality in their respective places of above enjoying free air, light and good hygienic condition. In the said purely residential area now the defendants have decided to establish a well organised in shape and size bakery, Industry/Factory on the CS plot No. 861 for production of biscuits, cakes, loafs and confectioneries of the various types and kinds instead of permanently removing from the said locality. The continuing one on the CS plot No.865 which the defendant Nos. 3-5 were verbally promised-bound to remove for good on the repeated demand there for made by the plaintiff and other residents of the locality. For that illegal and in view they have started to construct a furnace (চুল্লি) on the said CS plot No.861 and they are about to complete the same for the production of confectionery goods, various kinds of chemicals like ammonia, baking powder and raw materials including atta/flour, rotten eggs, sugar and "Mawa' (rotten water) are required to be used being mingled together for being rotten and decomposed for the purpose of production of the aforesaid items of bakery from the furnace, the brick built fire place, which will day and night generate and emit heat, smoke, bad smell and undesirable noise polluting the wholesome pure air and good hygienic condition creating nauseating obnoxious vexatious and noisy atmosphere constituting private and public nuisance germinating bacteria of various diseases for the plaintiff, his family members, patients attending his residence and clinic and other residents of the locality at large materially and substantially disturbing and interfering with physical and mental comforts of ordinary human living according to the plain, simple and sober notions of living causing annoyance, inconvenience, discomfort materially affecting the health and living condition of the plaintiff, his family members and other residents of the locality besides aggravating the ailments and suffering of the patients daily attending his clinic and residence materially affecting the congenial atmosphere of treatment given by-the plaintiff physician causing serious setback to the efficient performance of his professional duties relating to human life telling upon his profession and the well-being of the patients. The plaintiff further asserted in his plaint that the defendant Nos. 3-5 or all the defendants have no lawful right whatsoever, either to continue the aforesaid Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No. 865 or to start another afresh on the CS plot No. 861 as stated in the 3rd schedule of the plaint repeating and continuing the aforesaid private and public nuisance disturbing and interfering with the physical and mental comforts affecting the health and living condition of the plaintiff, his family members, patients attending his clinic and residence, residents of the locality besides plaintiffs normal performance of duties as physician polluting the wholesome air creating nauseating obnoxious vexatious and bad smell and noisy atmosphere either by continuing the existing Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No. 865 or starting new one on the CS. Plot No.861 as aforesaid or by both. Rather, the plaintiff from all points of law, equity and natural justice has the lawful right to oppose the defendants in the matter and get their acts stopped permanently for all times to come. So the plaintiff has been compelled to come up with this suit on his own behalf and that of others of the locality in the representative manner. It is further asserted by the plaintiff in the plaint that another party attempted to establish such Bakery/Factory on the land situated in between the plaintiffs aforesaid residential building and the clinic which has been permanently stopped by a prohibitory permanent injunction granted by the learned Munsif of the 2nd Court. Brahmanbaria in Title Suit No. 12 of 1972 brought by the plaintiff. The distance between the suit property and the plots would not be more than 20 feet The Judgment and decree passed in that suit are dated 8-5-1972 and decree signed on 15-5-1972. The plaintiff further asserted that the distance between the plaintiffs residence and the existing Bakery/factory run by the defendant Nos. 3-5 on the CS plot No. 865 is 15 feet and that of the plaintiffs residence and the attempted one to be set up the CS plot No. 861 is 4 feet only. The distance between plaintiff's clinic from the existing Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No.865 and the attempted one to be set up on the CS plot No. 861 is respectively 100 and 90 feet. 

 4. The plaintiff further asserted that the defendants are making brick preparation to start functioning of Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No. 861 with the furnace which they are expected to complete within a week or so either with the continuation of the existing Bakery/Factory on. CS 865 or by way of Shifting of the same therefrom to the CS plot No. 861 or running the both, If they do so i.e by starting a new-Bakery/Factory on the cs plot No. 861 either by way of shifting of the existing one from the cs plot No. 865 or keeping the existing one continuing, the plaintiff shall be put to mental and physical discomfort of ordinary human living according to plain, simple and sober notions of living causing annoyance, inconvenience, materially and substantially affecting him in mind and physique besides causing discomfort to his profession aggravating the ailments of his patients instead of duration and giving germs of new disease putting him to suffer irreparable loss which cannot be compensated in terms of money. The acts complained of cannot be prevented otherwise than by an order of injunction from the court. So, from all points of law, equity, natural justice, balance of convenience and inconvenience the plaintiff has got not only a prima facie arguable case but also a good case on merit to get an order of injunction from the court restraining the defendants from continuing the existing Bakery/Factory on the cs plot No. 865 repeating and continuing the private and public nusisance as aforesaid and by starting a new Bakery/Factory on the CS plot No. 861 or within the vicinity of the said locality by granting a permanent injunction. The plaintiff therefore, further asserted that the defendants are bound to dismantle and remove all the structures/fixtures of the existing Bakery/Factory situated on the cs plot No. 865 and structures/fixtures including the furnace under construction on the CS plot No.86l. 

 5. With the aforesaid allegations the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 filed the aforesaid title suit for the principal relief that the suit be decreed granting permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 3-5 or all the defendants if required for ends of justice from continuing and repeating the private and public nuisance by continuing functioning of the existing Bakery/Factory known as "Shahin Bakery and Confectionery" situated on the cs plot No. 865 and all the defendants from starting another Bakery /Factory on the cs plot No.861 as stated in the 3rd schedule creating private and public nuisance or any other place within the residential area in the vicinity of the plaintiffs residence and the clinic. 

 6. Only the defendant No. 3, that is, the present petitioner, contested the said suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations of the plaint. The defendant asserted in his written statement that the concerned area is mainly a commercial and shopping area. The defendant has been running the said bakery with, the due licence from-the concerned authority which situates on the cs plot No. 865 within a distance of 10 feet from the residential building of the plaintiff Jar the last 15/16 years without any inconvenience to the plaintiff and the plaintiff never protested about the running of the said bakery. It does not cause any special .damage or invasion to the rights of the. plaintiff and the plaintiff did not obtain any permission from the prescribed authority before filing of the suit. The defendant established a new furnace on the cs plot No. 861 in the eastern side to the extreme south and started production long before the filing of the present suit by, the plaintiff. There is a 2 feet width municipal drain after the wall of the residential building of the plaintiff and thereafter 5 feet 2 inches high wall and there is a further 5 feet high wall at a distance of 4 feet 5 inches, and, thereafter, there is another wall. The defendant further asserted that the disputed furnace situated at a distance of 17 feet and 10 inches away from the residential building of the plaintiff and he never used any "mawa" in the production of his produces and there is no bad smell and noise as it is not a mechanical but hand operating factory. The natural gas is being used and there is no smoke. Besides, there are several shops, oil mill, printing press, several offices and residential hotel and also there are two big Bakeries/Factories namely Tripti Bakery and Baby Bakery within the vicinity much nearer to the plaintiffs residential building and chamber, Moreover, on both sides of the road there are shops and on the western side of which the chamber of the plaintiff situates, there are, about 15 bakery shops having their attached furnaces. The defendant further asserted that noise is being created from the mill, printing press, video shops, market, etc. The defendant further asserted in his written statement that the plaintiff filed the present suit with an ulterior motive on false facts without exhausting remedy as provided by special law and, as such, the suit is barred. 

 7. The learned trial Court after taking evidences and hearing arguments of both sides decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff by its judgment and decree dated 30-9-1991 (decree signed on 14-10-1991). The defendant No.3 that is the present petitioner, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree preferred Title Appeal No. 2 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Brahmanbaria. The said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Brahmanbaria on transfer and dismissed the same by his judgment and decree dated 21-7-1993 (decree signed on 28-7-1993) affirming those of the trial Court. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Brahmanbaria the present petitioner preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule impugning the said judgment and decree dated 21-7-1993. 

 8. Mr. SR Karmaker, the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner, was ill and as such Mr. Abu Bakar Siddique, the learned Advocate, appeared on behalf of Mr. SR Karmaker and argued the case for the defendant-petitioner. Mr.Siddique submits that the suit itself is incompetent for want of sanction as provided in section 91(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and the provision of sanction as com tern plated in section 91(1) of the Code is a mandatory one but unfortunately, both the courts below lost sight of this aspect of case and decreed the suit ignoring this mandatory provision of law. He, therefore, submits emphatically that the suit is nothing but still born suit which ought to have been dismissed on the ground of maintainability for non-compliance of the mandatory provisions of section 91 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in support of his submission he relies on the decision reported in 36 DLR 227. The learned Advocate further submits that it is a suit of public nuisance which is a criminal offence under section 278 of the Penal Code and one can bring either a criminal action or a civil action against a public nuisance. If a civil action is brought in that case the plaintiff must obtain prior sanction either from the Attorney General under section 91 of the Code of Civil Procedure or from the appropriate authority as contemplated in section 93 of the Civil Procedure Code. In the instant case although it is a case of public nuisance without special damage the plaintiff has failed to obtain sanction from the competent authority and/or from the Attorney General of Bangladesh and, as such, the suit is not at all maintainable. The learned Advocate further submits that no issue on maintainability was framed by the learned trial Court but however this question of maintainability was adverted to by the learned appellate Court below and he also ultimately submits that issue No. 5 also covers the same. The learned Advocate, however, submits that the finding of the learned appellate Court below on the question of maintainability is invalid and illegal inasmuch as in the instant case the whole cause of action of the plaintiffs suit exists on public nuisance but no where in the plaint or in evidence the plaintiff has asserted this position and in that view of the matter the suit is not maintainable as has been laid down in the case reported in 46 CWN 261. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case special damage was not claimed by the plaintiff and this question was not considered by both the courts below which caused miscarriage of justice and in that view of the matter also the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate further submits that it is asserted by the defendant petitioner in his written statement that the area in question is a commercial and shopping area and not a residential area as contended by the plaintiff opposite party No.1 in his plaint and it would be clear from the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 and from the evidence of DW 1 that the locality in question is a commercial and shopping area and not a residential area and thus the findings of the learned appellate Court below as well as the trial Court that the area in question is a residential area is not tenable and is against weight of evidence. The learned Advocate further submits that nuisance is a relative term and the facts which can be nuisance in a particular area cannot be a nuisance in an undeveloped slum area. He stated by way of illustration that what can be a nuisance in developed area of the town cannot be a nuisance in the underdeveloped area of the town. So the learned appellate Court below ought to have held that there are many shops and factories in the locality which has now become a developed part of the town as a commercial and industrial area. The learned Advocate further submits that injunction is an equitable relief and one must be alert in seeking such relief because delay defeats equity. In the instant case the defendant petitioner has been carrying on his business of the said bakery in plot No.865 for last 15/16 years but no complaint was made by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 and it is only when he has decided to shift the said Bakery/Factory from the cs plot No. 865 to cs plot No.861 which is at a great distance from the residential building of the plaintiffs he has filed the suit with an ulterior motive being envious of the business carried on by the defendant petitioner. The learned Advocate further submits that in the instant case not only there has been a delay in filing the suit but also the plaintiff is guilty of acquiescence. The learned Advocate finally submits that taking all the aspects of the case into consideration, even on merit, the plaintiff has no case at all and both the courts below taking erroneous view of law of public nuisance has illegally decreed the suit against the defendant petitioner. 

 9. Mr. TH Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the judgment and submits that the learned trial Court as well as the learned appellate Court below committed no error of law occasioning failure of justice in decreeing the suit and the same does not call for any interference by this Court. The learned Advocate further submits that both the courts below on proper consideration of the facts and circumstance of the case and materials on record passed the impugned judgments which cannot be assailed on any ground whatsoever. Mr.Khan further submits that in the plaint averments have been made clearly as to the creation of nuisance causing damage and invasion to the rights of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 by running Bakery/ Factory in question and the facts and circumstances as disclosed in the suit is very much maintainable in law. The learned Advocate further submits that in view of the facts and circumstances of the case as contained in the plaint and the reliefs sought for it is not at all necessary to seek permission from the Attorney-General as provided in section 91 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Khan, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff opposite party No.1, further submits that this very point was raised and the same has been correctly answered by the appellate Court below and the finding of the appellate Court below on that point cannot be assailed on any ground whatsoever. Mr. Khan further submits that the plaintiff is very much entitled to maintain the suit for the reliefs as prayed for in the suit. Mr. Khan further submits that since the running of the Bakery/Factory in question was creating nuisance and other health hazards to the plaintiff, including oozing of bad smell, both the courts below rightly decreed the suit. He further submits that the defendant petitioner has misconceived and misread the evidence of the plaintiffs witnesses including the plaintiff as to the existence of other bakeries, shops and markets. He further submits that in the nearby area there is no other factory/bakery, shop and market which create nuisance and other health hazards as caused by the defendant's bakery. Mr. Khan further submits that the plaintiff by adducing evidence clearly proved that running of the defendant's bakery was creating nuisance to the health of the plaintiff and the courts below correctly decreed the suit. The learned Advocate in this regard further submits that the defendant petitioner has got no right to create nuisance and health hazards to the plaintiff. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff raised an objection at the very initial stage of establishing the bakery in question in the residential area and thereby creating nuisance and other health hazards and the defendant petitioner initially agreed upon to shift his bakery /factory from the place in question but after killing time on such assurance ultimately did not do so and hence the plaintiff was compelled to institute the suit. Mr. Khan, then, submits with much force that the decree of mandatory injunction passed by the courts below is fully justified in view of the facts and circumstances of the case and for that purpose he relied on two decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42 and 14 BLD (AD) 242. The learned Advocate finally submits that the case reported in 36 DLR 227 has no manner of application in the instant case inasmuch as that was a case related to section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in that view of the matter that cannot have any manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. The learned Advocate further submits that principles of law as enunciated in the other decisions are good in view of the facts and circumstances of those cases but each case has to be decided on its own merits and those decisions have no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the instant case. 

 12. In order to give rise to an action in nuisance there must be interference with the use or enjoyment of land or of some rights over or in connection with it causing damage to the plaintiff. The forms of interference are innumerable. Noise, smell, pollution of air or water, are the most usual instances, but there are many others. 

 "We think it is clear that this suit will not lie. The plaintiff sues defendants for obstructing a public road without showing that he has sustained any particular inconvenience in consequence of the obstruction. If he can maintain this suit, arty member of the public can do so, and the defendant may be ruined by innumerable actions by persons who have not sustained a farthing of damage." 

 19. Keeping these principles of law in mind if we now examine the facts and circumstances vis-a-vis the submission made by the learned Advocates for both the sides it appears to me that the submissions of Mr. A B Siddique that the suit is incompetent for non-compliance of section 91(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure is absolutely misconceived. It appears that the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner lost sight of the fact that there are two kinds of nuisance namely, public nuisance and private nuisance and in case of public nuisance if a member of public wants to initiate a civil proceeding it is incumbent upon him to obtain sanction under section 91(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in the absence of special damage. But if a plaintiff wants to bring an action against the defendant for his unlawful action on the land causing a private nuisance the power of section 91(1) cannot be invoked because in case of private nuisance no special damage is required to be proved by the plaintiff and if the plaintiff can prove that by the unlawful user of the land by the defendant some annoyance is caused to the plaintiff then he is entitled to get a relief and in that view of the matter the first submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioner that the instant suit is incompetent for want of sanction is not tenable in law as the instant action rests on private nuisance. 

 20. Mr. Siddique in course of his arguments referred to and relied on the case reported in AIR 1963 (Punjab) 104, and submitted that the plaintiff is not entitled to get an order of injunction inasmuch as he is guilty of inordinate delay in seeking the relief. The defendant started his bakery in cs plot No. 865 long 15 years ago but it is only when the defendant tried to shift his bakery on cs plot-No.861 the plaintiff initiated the present proceeding. No doubt it has been laid down in that decision that injunctive relief is available to those who show reasonable alertness in asking for equitable protection, and not to those who sleep over their rights. In that case the plaintiff after 34 years of service filed the suit disputing the date of retirement Moreover, it was observed in that case that if the court is satisfied that the circumstances of the case do not entitle the grant of perpetual injunction, a temporary injunction has to be refused. That was a service matter. The facts of that case has no manner of application in the facts of the present case. Besides, in the instant case it has been asserted by the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 that when the defendant petitioner was carrying on his manufacturing process of bakery/factory on the cs plot No.865 he raised objection and the defendant verbally assured the plaintiff that in future he would shift the bakery/factory from that place and the plaintiff relying on that assurance waited for certain period and when he found that the defendant petitioner is not keeping his assurance, he had no other alternative but to file the instant suit, not only to prohibit the defendant from carrying on his business on cs plot No.865 but also with a view to preventing him from carrying on his business on cs plot No. 861. In that view of the matter it cannot be said that the plaintiff allowed the defendant to carry 9n his bakery business for long 15 years, rather he was misled in the instant case by false assurance given by the defendant petitioner, Moreover, in the instant case the private nuisance complained of is a continuing one and in that view of the matter also the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 is entitled to ask for such relief as prayed for. In this connection it may also be noted that in that case it has been laid down, amongst others, that 

 So this decision in fact does not support the case of the defendant petitioners, rather supports the case of the plaintiff opposite party. 

 21. Similarly, the case reported in AIR 1929 (All) 877 also does not help Mr. Siddique. In that case it was found as a fact that the delay was deliberate on the part of the plaintiff and that for an improper motive and in that view of the matter injunction was refused. The facts of the present case are quite distinguishable from the facts of that case and it is not attracted in the present case. 

 22. In this connection it may also be stated that while discussing about the case reported in AIR 1963 (Punjab) 104, I have already pointed out that in the instant case neither there is any acquiescence nor deliberate delay on the part of the plaintiff and in that view of the matter no occasion arose for the courts below to refuse the reliefs prayed for by the plaintiff on that count. 

 23. Mr. Siddique the learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioner referred to and relied on the decision reported in AIR 1937 (Mad) 21 and submitted that the plaintiff is not entitled to get an order of injunction. In that case it has been held that a person is entitled to enjoy his own property as he pleases provided he does not create nuisance or interfere with rights of others. No injunction can be granted when there is no nuisance or interference with rights or apprehension thereof. I do not understand how this decision helps the defendant petitioner rather it helps the plaintiff opposite party No.1. In the present case there is positive assertion by the plaintiff opposite party No.1 of creation of nuisance by the defendant petitioner which interferes with the comfort of the plaintiff opposite party and both the courts below as of fact found that the nuisance created by the defendant petitioner caused discomforts to the plaintiff and the members of his family. 

 25. Nobody disputes the principles of law enunciated in this decision. In fact it helps the plaintiff. Fact of the case is that a factory was set up in a locality which is both an industrial and a residential locality. The whole of the locality was full of shops and godowns for storage of grain and other commodities and there were a number of mills spread allover. It was only the upper floors of the buildings which were used for residential purposes. Yet the factory owner was restrained by an order of injunction and stopped the running of the mill at night between the hours of 10-00 PM and 6-00 AM  and in my view this case also does not help the defendant petitioner, rather it goes in favour of the plaintiff opposite party No.1 inasmuch as both the courts below after taking into consideration the material and evidences on record have concurrently found that by establishing the bakery/factory on cs plot No. 865 the defendant petitioner is causing private nuisance to the plaintiff opposite party No.1 and the members of his family. . 

 26. Mr. Siddique also referred to another decision reported in AIR 1941 (Nagpur) 364 and submitted that in order to succeed in an action for nuisance the plaintiff must prove that he has some personal interest in the matter and secondly, that the alleged nuisance caused substantial discomfort or inconvenience. In that case the main allegation of the plaintiff was that under the building bye-laws in force no permission to erect a building could validly be given by the civil station sub-committee rules (1) the area of the plot built upon is not less than acre, (2) the bungalow is centrally located, (3) that it should be at least 80' away from the main building on the adjacent land, and (4) the facing of the building, its conservancy arrangements and the position of the outhouses are in confirmity with the existing arrangement of the buildings in that part of the civil station. It was averred that respondent No. 1 contravened the bye-laws in not confirming to the conditions laid down therein with the consequence that there was a likelihood of congestion and a consequent in sanitation and difficulty of drainage and diminution of light and ventilation and that the plaintiffs being in close proximity were affected by respondent's violation of the bye-law. The sanction granted by the civil station sub-committee in these circumstances was contended to be ultra vires of that body. It was found that the building which respondent No. 1 intended to erect was not contrary to the bye-laws and that the permission granted by the civil station sub-committee for the erection of the building was not ultra vires. It was also found that the building was not calculated to cause any discomfort, inconvenience or injury to the plaintiffs or their property. On these facts it was observed that as the appellants asked for an injunction restraining the building of the house it was incumbent on them under section 56(k), Specific Relief Act to show that they had some personal interest in the matter. It was also observed that in order to be an actionable nuisance there must be substantial interference with the comforts of the plaintiff. I do not understand how this case helps the defendant petitioner. The facts of this case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the instant case. In the instant case the plaintiff has substantial interest in the matter as he is the owner and possessor of the adjacent plot of the suit land. Moreover, the plaintiff has pleaded and proved by cogent evidence that the nuisance created by the defendant No.1 caused discomfort and inconvenience and injury to the plaintiff. Here 'we may profitably remember that to determine whether an act which is complained of as being a nuisance is strictly so or not is to be judged by the ordinary standards of persons residing in the neighborhood and the criterion would be the ordinary physical comfort of human existence according to plain, sober and simple notions obtaining amongst people and not according to the elegant and dainty modes and habits of living. It is not the standard of a petulant, cynical, hypersensitive or fastidious person that would furnish or guide but that of a person who expects to enjoy the ordinary comforts of a decent and healthy life in the local area where he resides. The inconvenience or discomfort must be of a substantial character to warrant legal interference. The opposite party No.1 has successfully fulfilled these criterions as both the courts concurrently found that the furnace generates and emits heat, smoke, bad smell and undesirable noise polluting the wholesome pure air and good hygienic condition. This case practically supports the case of the plaintiff opposite party No.1. 

 27. Mr. Siddique also relied on the case reported in 56 Indian Cases 571, where it was laid down that where a suit is in essence one for a perpetual Injunction with prayer for declaration ancillary thereto, the plaintiff must establish that the injunction is required to prevent the breach of an obligation and unless he does so, the injunction claimed-cannot be granted, more especially if equally efficacious relief can be obtained by any other usual mode of proceedings of the Code of Civil Procedure. This case also in my opinion actually helps the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 and not the defendant petitioner as the plaintiff, opposite party No. 1 has successfully proved his case in respect of private nuisance. 

 28. In the instant case it has been emphatically and unambiguously asserted by the plaintiff opposite party that business of bakery carried on by the defendant petitioner on the cs plot No. 865 emits heat, smoke, bad smell and undesirable noise which caused positive inconvenience to the health and comfort of the plaintiff and the residence of the plaintiff is to the contiguous west of the bakery/factory. 

 30. Mr. Siddique in course of his argument assailed the judgments of both the courts below and submitted that the courts below have committed gross illegality in passing a decree of mandatory injunction to demolish the chimney constructed on the CS plot No. 861 inasmuch as the chimney was erected prior to the filing of the suit. It appears from a perusal of the record that the suit was filed on 16-9-1989 and on that very day the plaintiff opposite party No.1 filed an application under Order 39 rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restraining the defendant from going on with the construction of the chimney on cs plot No. 861 and after hearing the parties the trial Court by order dated 16-9-1989 ordered the defendant petitioner to maintain status quo in respect of construction of chimney on cs plot No. 861. On the prayer of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 a local inspection of the aforesaid plot was held on 18-9-1989 and the learned Advocate Commissioner found that the construction of the chimney was going on and it was constructed on 18-9-1989 upto a height of 3 feet 1 inch. The plaintiff again on 9-1-1990 filed another application for inspection of the suit plot No. 861 and the learned Advocate Commissioner inspected the suit plot and submitted is report on 9-1-1990 and found the construction of chimney had been completed in the meantime and the height of chimney is 13 feet and 6 inches and circumference is 48 feet and 4 inches. 

 32. From a perusal of the impugned judgment it is crystal clear that the learned appellate Court below after taking into consideration all the legal aspects of the case as well as adverting to the relevant materials and evidence on record arrived at a definite finding that the plaintiff has been able to prove the case of private nuisance caused by the defendant petitioner and in that view of the matter has affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and there is concurrent finding on that point by both the courts below and in that view of the matter also the impugned judgment calls for no interference by this court. 

 33. Here it may be stated that in the instant case both the courts below also noticed that the act complained of also comes within the ambit of public nuisance but that has not vitiated the impugned judgment as it is found from the statements of the plaint that the plaintiff has categorically and specifically made out a case of private nuisance and has been able to prove the same by cogent evidence. 

 34. The plaintiffs action rests on private nuisance but the main branch of submission of Mr. Siddique is that it is a case of public nuisance and the plaintiff has failed to prove special damage and in that view of the matter besides non-compliance of section 91(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure the case is also not sustainable on merits. Mr. Siddique surely missed the point that in the law of torts there is private nuisance as well and the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 has successfully pleaded and proved the elements of private nuisance in the instant case. In that view of the matter the decision reported in 36 DLR 227 and the other decisions referred by Mr. Siddique in support of his contention are not relevant at all for proper disposal of the Rule.
